lessons.title: Neither … nor: Connecting Negative Alternatives
lessons.content: Neither … nor is used to connect the same kind of word or phrase in a sentence. Neither makes a negative statement about two people or things. It means 'not one and not the other'.

details.explanation: Use 'neither … nor' to join two negative alternatives. Both parts must be the same grammatical type.
details.example: I like neither banana nor apple.

details.explanation: When both clauses share the same subject, place 'neither' before the first verb and 'nor' before the second.
details.burmese: ကျပ် စော် အိ လူပ် စော် အိ လူပ်မျကျုံပ၌ဦး့

lessons.title: Subject-Verb Agreement with Neither … nor
lessons.content: If one subject is singular and the other is plural, the verb form agrees with the subject that is nearest to the verb. This rule is the same as with 'either … or'.

details.explanation: When the two subjects joined by 'neither … nor' differ in number, the verb takes the form of the nearer subject.
details.example: Neither my parents nor my brother likes pineapple.

details.concept: Neither I nor my friends + plural verb
details.explanation: When the nearest subject is plural, use the plural verb form.
details.example: Neither I nor my friends go to the party.
